Definition: apparently, a primary particle, having a copulative and sometimes also a cumulative force; and, also, even, so then, too, etc.; often used in connection (or composition) with other particles or small words:--and, also, both, but, even, for, if, or, so, that, then, therefore, when, yet.
BiblicalUsage: Kai is the little word that holds the New Testament together — 'and,' 'also,' 'even.' It joins clause to clause thousands of times, and sometimes it carries the weight itself: believe also in me; seek first the kingdom and all these things shall be added; how shall He not with Him also freely give us all things.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe this smallest of words teaches me that nothing in the gospel stands alone, for faith and obedience, promise and command, Christ and His people are joined by the 'and', and a gospel without its 'ands' would fall apart in my hands.
